\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مستقبل} (mustaqbil)}{مستقبل (mustaqbil)}]{\ur{مستقبل} (mustaqbil) — the future}

\label{lesson:UR-C145-mustaqbil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for last, then the Urdu for to happen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مستقبل}}
\textbf{\ur{مستقبل}} — \emph{mustaqbil} — \textquotedblleft{}the future\textquotedblright{}. Urdu's future adds \textbf{\ur{گا}}, \textbf{\ur{گی}} or \textbf{\ur{گے}} to the verb's \emph{-ūṅ} form: \textbf{\ur{میں} \ur{پڑھوں} \ur{گا۔}} — \emph{maiṅ paṛhūṅgā} — \textquotedblleft{}I will read.\textquotedblright{} A woman says \textbf{\ur{پڑھوں} \ur{گی}}, \emph{paṛhūṅgī}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mustaqbil}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mustaqbil}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mustaqbil}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for last, then the Urdu for to happen, then say \emph{mustaqbil} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آئندہ} (āindā)}{آئندہ (āindā)}]{\ur{آئندہ} (āindā) — next, in future}

\label{lesson:UR-C145-ainda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to happen, then the Urdu for the future.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آئندہ}}
\textbf{\ur{آئندہ}} — \emph{āindā} — \textquotedblleft{}next, in future\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{آئندہ} \ur{ہفتے}} — \emph{āindā hafte} — \textquotedblleft{}next week\textquotedblright{}. On its own it means \textquotedblleft{}from now on\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\ur{آئندہ} \ur{ایسا} \ur{نہ} \ur{کرنا۔}} — \emph{āindā aisā na karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}Don't do that again.\textquotedblright{}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جلد} \ur{ہی} (jald hī)}{جلد ہی (jald hī)}]{\ur{جلد} \ur{ہی} (jald hī) — soon}

\label{lesson:UR-C145-jald-hi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the future, then the Urdu for next.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جلد} \ur{ہی}}
\textbf{\ur{جلد} \ur{ہی}} — \emph{jald hī} — \textquotedblleft{}soon\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{جلد}} has two readings: \emph{jild}, \textquotedblleft{}skin\textquotedblright{} or \textquotedblleft{}a volume\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{jald}, \textquotedblleft{}quickly\textquotedblright{}. Here it is \emph{jald}, with the emphatic \textbf{\ur{ہی}}: \textbf{\ur{وہ} \ur{جلد} \ur{ہی} \ur{آئے} \ur{گا۔}} — \emph{voh jald hī āegā} — \textquotedblleft{}He will come soon.\textquotedblright{}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پروگرام} (progrām)}{پروگرام (progrām)}]{\ur{پروگرام} (progrām) — a plan, a programme}

\label{lesson:UR-C145-program}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for next, then the Urdu for soon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پروگرام}}
\textbf{\ur{پروگرام}} — \emph{progrām} — \textquotedblleft{}a plan, a programme\textquotedblright{}. From English \emph{programme}, and the everyday word for a plan: \textbf{\ur{کل} \ur{کا} \ur{پروگرام} \ur{بناتے} \ur{ہیں۔}} — \emph{kal kā progrām banāte haiṅ} — \textquotedblleft{}Let's make a plan for tomorrow.\textquotedblright{}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{طے} \ur{کرنا} (tai karnā)}{طے کرنا (tai karnā)}]{\ur{طے} \ur{کرنا} (tai karnā) — to decide, to settle}

\label{lesson:UR-C145-tai-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for soon, then the Urdu for a plan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{طے} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{طے} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{tai karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to decide, to settle\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{ہم} \ur{نے} \ur{طے} \ur{کیا} \ur{کہ} ...} — \emph{ham ne tai kiyā ki} — \textquotedblleft{}We decided that ...\textquotedblright{} The past of \textbf{\ur{کرنا}} is \textbf{\ur{کیا}}.
